---
title: "Spatial Clustering Explorer"
date: 2026-09-09
categories: [tool, geoml]
description: "Upload a point dataset and find spatial clusters with DBSCAN — set a distance radius and a minimum group size, see clusters colored on the map, and download the result. Runs entirely in your browser, powered by Python."
page-layout: full
---

Upload a point file — `.geojson`, or a shapefile as a single `.zip` or
as `.shp`/`.dbf`/`.shx` selected together — set a distance radius
(ε) and a minimum group size, and find which points cluster together
in space. Points that don't belong to any dense-enough group are
marked as noise, not forced into the nearest cluster.

::: {.callout-tip}
**Private by design.** Your file is processed entirely in your
browser (Python via WebAssembly) — it's never uploaded to any server,
including ours. Nothing to configure, nothing to trust: the code
never gets the chance to see your data.
:::

```{ojs}
mutable uploadStatus = WebGeoDS.Upload.defaultStatus
mutable uploadBusy = false
```


```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
{
  // Python-only tool (see the article for the same computation shown
  // in R too): skip writing to R's filesystem entirely, so selecting
  // a file doesn't also load webR in the background for no reason.
  mutable uploadBusy = true;
  mutable uploadStatus = "⌛ Uploading...";
  try {
    const result = await WebGeoDS.Upload.load(uploadedFiles, { languages: ["python"] });
    if (result.ok) {
      mutable uploadStatus = "⌛ Inspecting...";
      await autoInspect();
      mutable uploadStatus = result.message;
    } else {
      mutable uploadStatus = result.message;
    }
  } finally {
    mutable uploadBusy = false;
  }
}
```

The code itself isn't shown here — it's a fixed, non-editable
computation using scikit-learn's DBSCAN underneath. Want to see it
built up step by step, in Python *and* R? Read
[Finding Spatial Clusters with DBSCAN](/posts/spatial-clustering.html).

```{.webgeods-python #spatial-clustering-inspect-py}
#| package: geopandas
import geopandas as gpd

def export_crs(g):
    # Reprojects `g` back to the CRS it was UPLOADED in (original_crs,
    # set below and reused as a module-level global by the compute
    # cell) -- every downloadable result goes through this, even
    # though the map/clustering above always work in WGS84 (GeoJSON
    # and MapLibre both assume it). Same pattern as this project's
    # other vector tools (e.g. the Validator).
    if g is None or original_crs is None or str(original_crs) == "EPSG:4326":
        return g
    return g.to_crs(original_crs)

EMPTY_FC = {"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": []}

# No built-in fallback: if nothing is readable, gdf stays None and the
# result is an empty FeatureCollection -- this cell only ever runs
# after a successful upload or "Load example".
gdf = None
for path in ["/uploaded.geojson", "/uploaded.shp", "/vsizip//uploaded.zip"]:
    try:
        gdf = gpd.read_file(path)
        break
    except Exception:
        pass

crs_warning = None
original_crs = None
summary_out = None
if gdf is not None:
    if gdf.crs is None:
        gdf = gdf.set_crs("EPSG:4326")
        crs_warning = "No CRS found in the uploaded file — assuming WGS84 (EPSG:4326)."
    original_crs = gdf.crs
    if str(original_crs) != "EPSG:4326":
        gdf = gdf.to_crs("EPSG:4326")

    summary_out = {
        "count": int(len(gdf)),
        "crs": str(original_crs)
    }

{
    "features": gdf.__geo_interface__ if gdf is not None else EMPTY_FC,
    "crsWarning": crs_warning,
    "summary": summary_out
}
```

```{ojs}
}
```

```{ojs}
// Same "match" expression clusterPaint() used to build by hand,
// generalized as shared/ui.js's matchPaint() (also handles the empty
// clusterIds case the comment used to explain here -- see its own
// doc comment).
clusterPaint = (clusterIds) =>
  WebGeoDS.matchPaint(clusterIds, "cluster", { fallback: NOISE_COLOR })
```

```{.webgeods-python #spatial-clustering-compute-py}
#| inject: [epsMeters, minPts]
#| package: geopandas, scikit-learn
import numpy as np
from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN

# Reuses the WGS84 `gdf` already read and CRS-normalized by the
# inspect cell above (same session -- same pattern as the Validator's
# Fix button reusing its own diagnose cell's `gdf`), rather than
# re-reading the file.
gdf_calc = gdf.copy()

# Working/calculation CRS: DBSCAN's eps is a real distance, so
# clustering must run on projected (metric) coordinates, never
# degrees -- same reasoning, same UTM auto-pick formula, as this
# project's Viewshed tool (raster-viewshed.qmd). Picked from the
# uploaded data's own bounding-box center (not a per-feature centroid
# mean -- that would make GeoPandas warn that "centroid" is unreliable
# in a geographic CRS, a real warning for polygons even though it's a
# false alarm for the point data this tool expects; total_bounds sidesteps
# it entirely and matches Viewshed's own extent-center pattern): a
# reasonable default for a single local dataset, not a universally
# correct choice for data spanning multiple UTM zones, near the poles,
# or very large extents.
minx, miny, maxx, maxy = gdf_calc.total_bounds
center_lon = float((minx + maxx) / 2)
center_lat = float((miny + maxy) / 2)
utm_zone = int((center_lon + 180) // 6) + 1
calc_epsg = 32600 + utm_zone if center_lat >= 0 else 32700 + utm_zone
calc_crs_label = f"EPSG:{calc_epsg}"

gdf_proj = gdf_calc.to_crs(epsg=calc_epsg)
proj_x = gdf_proj.geometry.centroid.x.to_numpy()
proj_y = gdf_proj.geometry.centroid.y.to_numpy()

# A single UTM zone distorts badly -- to the point of returning inf --
# for points far enough from it. Fitting on infinite coordinates fails
# deep inside scikit-learn with an opaque error (the same failure mode
# found and fixed in the Spatial Classifier tool); drop those points
# here instead, with a clear message if too few remain.
finite_mask = np.isfinite(proj_x) & np.isfinite(proj_y)
excluded_count = int((~finite_mask).sum())
if not finite_mask.any():
    raise ValueError(
        f"None of the {len(gdf_calc)} points could be projected into a "
        f"single UTM zone ({calc_crs_label}) -- this dataset spans too wide "
        "an area for this tool's single-zone approach. Try a smaller, more "
        "local file."
    )
gdf_calc = gdf_calc[finite_mask].copy()
coords = np.column_stack([proj_x[finite_mask], proj_y[finite_mask]])

# scikit-learn's DBSCAN labels noise as -1 -- a real point of
# divergence from R's dbscan package (which uses 0), covered in the
# companion article rather than papered over here.
labels = DBSCAN(eps=float(epsMeters), min_samples=int(minPts)).fit(coords).labels_
gdf_calc["cluster"] = [int(l) for l in labels]

cluster_ids = sorted(int(c) for c in set(labels) if c != -1)
n_noise = int((labels == -1).sum())

{
    "features": gdf_calc.__geo_interface__,
    "originalCrsFeatures": export_crs(gdf_calc).__geo_interface__,
    "summary": {
        "calculationCrs": calc_crs_label,
        "clusterIds": cluster_ids,
        "clusterCount": len(cluster_ids),
        "noiseCount": n_noise,
        "totalCount": int(len(gdf_calc)),
        "excludedCount": excluded_count
    }
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| output: false
// The ε/min-points inputs + Compute button, rebuilt whenever
// inspectSummary changes -- same "disabled with an explanatory
// message until there's data" pattern as Raster Calculator's own
// band-math row.
clusterControlsRow = {
  const s = inspectSummary;
  const row = document.createElement("div");
  row.className = "webgeods-panel-row";

  if (!s) {
    const status = document.createElement("span");
    status.className = "webgeods-panel-status";
    status.textContent = "Upload a point file or load the example to set parameters.";
    row.append(status);
    return row;
  }

  const label = (text) => {
    const span = document.createElement("span");
    span.className = "webgeods-panel-status";
    span.textContent = text;
    return span;
  };

  const makeNumberInput = (id, defaultValue, step, min, width) => {
    const input = document.createElement("input");
    input.type = "number";
    input.id = id;
    input.step = String(step);
    input.min = String(min);
    input.value = String(defaultValue);
    input.className = "webgeods-panel-status";
    input.style.width = width;
    return input;
  };

  const epsInput = makeNumberInput("eps-input", 100, 10, 1, "70px");
  const minPtsInput = makeNumberInput("min-pts-input", 5, 1, 1, "50px");

  const computeButton = document.createElement("button");
  computeButton.className = "webgeods-panel-btn";
  computeButton.textContent = "▶ Compute";
  computeButton.onclick = async () => {
    computeButton.disabled = true;
    const originalText = computeButton.textContent;
    computeButton.textContent = "⌛ Clustering...";
    try {
      const epsMeters = Number(epsInput.value);
      const minPts = Number(minPtsInput.value);
      window.epsMeters = epsMeters;
      window.minPts = minPts;
      await window.WebGeoDS.CodeCell.find("spatial-clustering-compute-py").run();
      const result = document.getElementById("spatial-clustering-compute-py").value;
      await sharedMap.setGeoJSON("spatial-clustering-py", result.features, {
        paint: clusterPaint(result.summary.clusterIds)
      });
      mutable exportFeatures = result.originalCrsFeatures;
      mutable resultSummary = { ...result.summary, epsMeters, minPts };
      window.WebGeoDS.track?.("validation_completed", { tool: "spatial-clustering-explorer" });
    } catch (err) {
      console.error("spatial-clustering-explorer: Compute failed", err);
      mutable uploadStatus = `⚠️ Compute failed: ${err.message}`;
    } finally {
      computeButton.disabled = false;
      computeButton.textContent = originalText;
    }
  };

  row.append(
    label("ε (eps, meters):"), epsInput,
    label("min points:"), minPtsInput,
    computeButton
  );
  return row;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
```
```{ojs}
statCard = {
  const s = inspectSummary;
  const r = resultSummary;

  if (!s) {
    return WebGeoDS.statCard([
      ["Points", "—"],
      ["—", "Upload a point GeoJSON/Shapefile or load the example above"]
    ]);
  }

  const rows = [
    ["Points", s.count.toLocaleString()],
    ["Original CRS", s.crs === "None" || !s.crs ? "Unknown" : s.crs]
  ];

  if (r) {
    rows.push(["Calculation CRS", r.calculationCrs]);
    if (r.excludedCount > 0) {
      rows.push(["Excluded from clustering", `${r.excludedCount} (too far from the calculation UTM zone to project)`]);
    }
    rows.push(["ε (eps)", `${r.epsMeters} m`]);
    rows.push(["Min points", r.minPts]);
    rows.push(["Clusters found", r.clusterCount]);
    rows.push(["Noise points", r.noiseCount]);
  }

  return WebGeoDS.statCard(rows);
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
legendEl = {
  const r = resultSummary;
  if (!r) return WebGeoDS.legend(null);

  const items = r.clusterIds.map((id, i) => ({
    color: CLUSTER_PALETTE[i % CLUSTER_PALETTE.length],
    label: `Cluster ${id}`
  }));
  if (r.noiseCount > 0) items.push({ color: NOISE_COLOR, label: "Noise" });

  return WebGeoDS.legend(items);
}
```
